Information since June continues to signal strong real activity and a tight labor market, consistent with the FOMC’s statement. The Beige Book reinforces this with widespread reports of difficulty finding qualified workers across occupations (e.g., engineers, manufacturing and IT workers, truck drivers), firms converting temporary to permanent staff and enhancing compensation/benefits, and some increases in work hours—pointing to broadening but uneven wage pressures by sector. Most Districts reported rising prices and expect pricing pressures to intensify, while consumer spending remained solid in Richmond and Dallas (with Dallas supported by the energy sector). Offsetting factors include signs that higher interest rates are weighing on existing home sales and mixed movements in some agricultural commodity prices. Overall, conditions remain positive with inflation near 2 percent but edging firmer; the balance of evidence supports continued gradualism and vigilance rather than acceleration.
